display.purpose: The reader’s session title, and nothing else.

wordmark.purpose: The rail wordmark and error-state headings.

body.purpose: Reading prose in the conversation reader. The one role that sets at 400.

control.purpose: The workhorse: toolbar buttons, list labels, form controls.

data.purpose: Times, durations, token counts, shas, line counts, paths. Mono, tabular.

figure.purpose: The digest’s lead figure. Mono at display scale — the one number the Insight job leads with.

shadows.name: lift-1
shadows.purpose: Detail cards, the selected block, the selected lane bar. The only elevation in use.

shadows.name: lift-2
shadows.purpose: Reserved for a surface floating above a pane. Currently referenced nowhere — spend it deliberately or delete it.

motion.name: motion-state
motion.purpose: The response to a pointer or a toggle.

motion.name: motion-live
motion.purpose: The only repeating animation in the app: the footer dot while a collector runs. Allowed because something is happening now and will stop on its own.

motion.name: entrance
motion.purpose: Both authored entrances — the 620ms staggered lane reveal and the reader’s 260ms settle.

motion.name: lane-reveal
motion.purpose: Reveals rather than scales: scaleX deformed the end marks and hatch pitch of the evidence treatments.

components.name: Lane Bar — from sessions
components.description: A block whose span a conversation brackets. Solid, because the whole span is evidenced.
components.css: .ds-lane { position: relative; height: 40px; background: var(--ground, #0b0c0f); } .ds-bar { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 8%; width: 60%; height: 23px; transform: translateY(-50%); border-radius: 4px; --ink: rgba(255,255,255,0.36); --ink-bed: rgba(255,255,255,0.11); cursor: pointer; } .ds-bar-sessions { background: var(--ink); } .ds-bar-sessions:hover { --ink: rgba(255,255,255,0.54); }

components.name: Lane Bar — from commits
components.description: Exact at the commits, inferred between them. The hatch claims no positions.
components.css: .ds-bar-commits { background-color: var(--ink-bed); background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, var(--ink) 0 2px, transparent 2px 6px); } .ds-bar-commits:hover { --ink: rgba(255,255,255,0.54); --ink-bed: rgba(255,255,255,0.2); }

components.name: Lane Bar — from saves
components.description: Two mtimes and nothing known between. The ends are marked because the ends are what the archive has.
components.css: .ds-bar-saves { --ink: var(--amber, #f2a93b); --ink-link: color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber, #f2a93b) 52%, transparent); background-image: linear-gradient(var(--ink-link), var(--ink-link)); background-repeat: no-repeat; background-position: center; background-size: 100% 3px; } .ds-bar-saves::before, .ds-bar-saves::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; width: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--ink); } .ds-bar-saves::before { left: 0; } .ds-bar-saves::after { right: 0; }

components.name: Lane Bar — from records only
components.description: Records the timeline cannot itemise. The span is real; nothing in it is describable, so it claims no ends.
components.css: .ds-bar-bare { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--ink) 0 3px, transparent 3px 7px); background-repeat: no-repeat; background-position: center; background-size: 100% 3px; }

components.name: Lane Bar — selected
components.description: Selection takes the ink, never the shape. A selected saves-only block is still a pair of end marks.
components.css: .ds-bar-on { --ink: var(--accent, #e93d97); --ink-bed: rgba(233,61,151,0.16); --ink-link: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent, #e93d97) 72%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4), 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.28); }

components.name: Rail Row
components.description: Scope, category and project rows in the vibrancy rail. Selection is a flat accent fill with a legible edge — never a glow.
components.html: <nav class="ds-rail"><button class="ds-rail-row">This week</button><button class="ds-rail-row ds-rail-row-on">This month</button></nav>
components.css: .ds-rail { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.022); padding: 8px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; } .ds-rail-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; width: 100%; padding: 7px 8px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: none; color: var(--text-dim, #a2a8b6); font: 520 14.5px/1.35 -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms ease-out, color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-rail-row:hover { background: var(--surface-hover, #1f2330); color: var(--text, #edeef2); } .ds-rail-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e93d97); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-rail-row-on { background: rgba(233,61,151,0.16); color: var(--text, #edeef2); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(233,61,151,0.42); }

components.name: View Toggle
components.description: The segmented Lanes/Stream switch in the toolbar. The selected icon turns accent.
components.css: .ds-views { display: inline-flex; gap: 2px; padding: 2px; border-radius: 9px; background: var(--surface, #12141a); } .ds-view { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 5px 11px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: none; color: var(--text-dim, #a2a8b6); font: 560 14px/1.4 -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms ease-out, color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-view:hover { color: var(--text, #edeef2); } .ds-view:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e93d97); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-view-on { background: rgba(233,61,151,0.16); color: var(--text, #edeef2); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(233,61,151,0.42); }

components.name: Filter Field
components.description: The toolbar filter. Focus shifts the border to the accent edge.
components.html: <label class="ds-filter"><input class="ds-filter-input" type="text" placeholder="Filter projects, sessions, commits…" aria-label="Filter"></label>
components.css: .ds-filter { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; width: 320px; padding: 0 10px; height: 30px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--surface, #12141a); } .ds-filter:focus-within { border-color: rgba(233,61,151,0.42); } .ds-filter-input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; border: none; background: none; color: var(--text, #edeef2); font: 500 14px/1.4 -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-filter-input::placeholder { color: var(--text-faint, #878e9d); } .ds-filter-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e93d97); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Action Button
components.description: The one written button in the app: settings actions and error recovery. Never more than one strong variant in a group.
components.css: .ds-act { padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--surface-raised, #191c24); color: var(--text, #edeef2); font: 540 14px/1.4 -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms ease-out, color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-act:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--surface-hover, #1f2330); } .ds-act:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e93d97); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-act:disabled { opacity: 0.55; cursor: default; } .ds-act-strong { background: rgba(233,61,151,0.16); border-color: rgba(233,61,151,0.42); }

components.name: Confidence Label
components.description: The system’s signature on the attribution axis. A closed ring for a witnessed claim, the same ring broken for an inferred one.
components.html: witnessed inferred
components.css: .ds-tier { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; font: 500 13.5px/1.45 -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-tier-certain { color: var(--add, #56c98a); } .ds-tier-inferred { color: var(--amber, #f2a93b); }

components.css: .ds-digest { display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 11px 18px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.07); background: var(--ground, #0b0c0f); font: 500 13.5px/1.45 -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--text-faint, #878e9d); } .ds-digest span { white-space: nowrap; } .ds-digest b { color: var(--text, #edeef2); font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-weight: 620; font-size: 13.5px; } .ds-digest-time { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: 2px 18px; } .ds-lead { font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-dim, #a2a8b6); } .ds-big { font-size: 19px; font-weight: 640; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-mid { font-size: 15px; } .ds-split { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 2px 14px; margin: 3px 0 0; } .ds-split b { font-weight: 560; } .ds-census { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px 18px; margin-top: 9px; } .ds-census b { color: var(--text-dim, #a2a8b6); }

narrative.northStar: The instrument panel that shows its own confidence — dense, dark, one accent, and never a figure it cannot support.
narrative.overview: lore reads what other systems leave behind and keeps it after they delete it. The interface exists to make an uneven record legible without smoothing it, so the governing idea is not an aesthetic but a discipline: every figure on screen carries how it was established. The discipline has to hold at the top as well as at the leaf. It is easy to grade a single commit and then present a week as one confident number; for a while this build did exactly that, annotating every detail while the two surfaces a person actually lands on — the digest and the lane bars — said nothing about their own footing. Both now carry it: the bars in their fill, the digest in a split that adds up. The system is dark only, and by decision rather than by category habit — this is read at a desk, on the machine that produced the work, usually late. Its restraint is the restraint of an instrument panel: one accent, no ornament, dense information set at sizes that stay comfortable for a long look.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only, by decision rather than default
One accent, magenta, because git owns red and green and amber is reserved for uncertainty
Real macOS window vibrancy on the scope rail only; dense content on solid ground
Every span states what kind of record backs it
Two separate axes — attribution and evidence — that never share a vocabulary
A 13px type floor and a 500 weight floor for interface text; reading prose alone sets at 400
Time as lanes of real projects on a real axis, never a calendar grid or a contribution heatmap

rules.name: The Two Axes Rule
rules.body: Attribution asks who made a change and speaks in ring icons and the green/amber pair. Evidence asks what kind of record backs a span and speaks in the fill of a lane bar and the split under the digest. A colour or a word borrowed across the two collapses both. Amber is the one deliberate overlap: it means uncertainty on either axis.

rules.name: The Two Floors Rule
rules.body: Interface text never goes below weight 500 — labels, controls, rail rows, metadata, figures. Reading prose sets at 400, and only in the conversation reader and the markdown it renders. A 400 weight anywhere outside a reading surface is a defect.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Selection takes the ink, never the shape. A selected saves-only block is still visibly a pair of end marks in magenta, not a solid claim. Any state that flattens a treatment into a rectangle has destroyed the only thing the treatment was there to say.

rules.name: The Legible Mark Rule
rules.body: Every mark that carries a class clears 3:1 against ground on its own. A hatch bed is exempt because its strokes carry identity; a connector is not, because without it two end marks are two unrelated dots.

dos: Do show how a claim was established, next to the claim.
Do keep magenta for selection and live state; keep amber for uncertainty.
Do set data in the mono token with tabular numerals.
Do say what a surface does hold when it cannot show what was expected.
Do give a raised surface a shadow with offset and blur.
Do let a mark that carries meaning clear 3:1 against its ground on its own.
Do split a figure only where the parts add up. Elapsed does not; across-projects does.
donts: Don’t set interface type below 13px or below weight 500. Reading prose is the one exception and sets at 400.
Don’t use the accent as a glow, a gradient, or a decorative fill.
Don’t extend vibrancy beyond the scope rail, or add blur for atmosphere.
Don’t render a calendar grid or a contribution heatmap as a primary view.
Don’t print a figure lore cannot support — no 0m for a real block, no clock range without dates across days, no total where the data only supports a floor, no digest over a range holding nothing.
Don’t introduce a second accent, or let a category hue carry state.
Don’t put a category hue back on a lane bar. The group heading above it and the rail row that filtered to it already say it; the fill is spent on evidence now.
Don’t borrow a word or a colour across the attribution and evidence axes.
Don’t animate a bar with a transform that deforms the marks inside it.
